name: Kokusai-dori and Makishi
description: Kokusai-dori is Naha's roughly two-kilometre main avenue lined with shops, restaurants, bars and hotels, with the covered Makishi Public Market and Heiwa-dori arcades just off it. It is the most central, walkable and amenity-rich area for visitors.
bestFor: Travellers wanting central hotels, dining, nightlife and easy transport

name: Omoromachi (Shintoshin)
description: Omoromachi, in the Shintoshin new city centre, is a planned modern district with the Okinawa Prefectural Museum, department stores, DFS Galleria, and tidy wide streets. Served by its own monorail station, it feels newer and calmer than Kokusai-dori.
bestFor: Visitors wanting modern amenities, shopping and a calmer, newer area

name: Shuri
description: Shuri sits on higher ground in eastern Naha around Shuri Castle, the former royal seat of the Ryukyu Kingdom. Quieter and more residential, it holds historic gates, stone-paved lanes, temples and monorail access, offering a slower, heritage-focused base.
bestFor: History lovers wanting a calm residential base near castle sights

name: Naminoue and Nishi
description: The Naminoue and Nishi area on Naha's western waterfront holds Naminoue Beach, the clifftop Naminoue Shrine and the nearby port for ferries to outer islands. It is the closest swimmable beach to the city centre, with a relaxed seaside feel.
bestFor: Travellers wanting a beach and shrine within walking distance of town
